linked_issues.title: A cancelled foreground supersedes=True handler loses all of its state writes under StateManagerRedis but keeps them under the in-memory manager

unresolved.first_comment: Please add one sentence here: a write the cancelled handler makes after its last `yield` (for example in its `except asyncio.CancelledError` cleanup) is stored, but the frontend receives it only with a later update that touches the same var. Evidence: the disk and memory managers keep the dirty-var bookkeeping on the live state object, so the replacement handler's next delta carries that write. Redis rebuilds the bookkeeping on unpickle (`_init_bookkeeping` in `__setstate__`), so the replacement handler's delta does not include it. Repro: a `@rx.event(supersedes=True)` handler sets `self.entries` before the `yield` and sets `Child.last_cancelled` only in its `except asyncio.CancelledError` block. After the replacement handler completes on Redis, the page shows `entries` with the cancelled handler's values, but `Child.last_cancelled` stays empty until a page reload. The same app on the disk state manager shows `Child.last_cancelled` right away. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

outstanding_asks.ask: Shield the Redis save so a second cancellation cannot interrupt persistence and drop state.
Document that a cancelled handler's post-yield cleanup write is persisted by Redis but may not reach the frontend until a later update touches the same var.
